**Observations from the image:**

- **Affected part**: Wheat spike/head (spikelets and glumes)
- **Color**: Prominent orange/salmon-pink discoloration and apparent fungal sporulation on the spikelets; upper portion of the head shows bleached/straw-colored glumes
- **Texture/Pattern**: Spikelets are partially collapsed and covered with an orange-pink mycelial/spore mass; dark necrosis visible at some glume bases
- **Other cues**: Some spikelets remain green while others are fully bleached — the classic "partial bleaching" pattern

**Reasoning:**

The orange-pink fungal sporulation (Fusarium conidia/mycelium) covering the spikelets, combined with premature bleaching of the upper portion of the wheat head and partial head involvement, is the hallmark presentation of **Fusarium Head Blight (Head Scab)**. The salmon/orange color specifically reflects *Fusarium* sporulation on the rachis and glumes. This distinguishes it from:
- **Loose Smut**: Dark brown-black powdery spore mass replacing the entire head
- **Stem/Stripe/Leaf Rust**: Pustules on vegetative tissue (leaves/stems), not the head
- **Dwarf Bunt**: Dark, fishy-smelling teliospore balls inside grains
